text:
**Findings**
| Severity | Location | Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| high | [evalmerge/ingest.py](/work/evalmerge/ingest.py:74) `74-89` | Re-ingesting changed input only upserts and never removes rows missing from the latest input tree, so stale results remain in reports. |
| high | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:254) `254` | Malformed XML raises `ET.ParseError` and crashes ingest instead of producing a structured warning. |
| high | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:110) `110-164, 202-245, 256-324` | Empty `run_id`, `model`, or `task` values are accepted; empty run IDs collide under `UNIQUE(run_id, source)` and silently overwrite rows. |
| high | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:114) `114-151, 203-232, 268-311` | Non-finite scores like `NaN` are treated as numeric and can abort ingest with a SQLite `NOT NULL` integrity error. |
| medium | [evalmerge/db.py](/work/evalmerge/db.py:70) `70-82` | `model_aliases` is append-only while warnings/stats are replaced, so alias reports can include stale spellings from prior ingests. |
| medium | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:87) `87-91` | Format A parses CSV one physical line at a time, corrupting valid CSV records with quoted embedded newlines. |
| medium | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:87) `87, 173` | CSV and JSONL inputs are read fully into memory, creating avoidable OOM/DoS risk for large harness outputs. |
| medium | [evalmerge/parsers.py](/work/evalmerge/parsers.py:203) `203-204` | Format B assumes truthy `metrics` is a dict; malformed JSON such as `"metrics": [1]` crashes with `AttributeError`. |
| low | [evalmerge/cli.py](/work/evalmerge/cli.py:44) `44-47` | Empty-directory ingest returns an error only after creating/mutating the SQLite database. |
| low | [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:5) `5-12` | Package metadata is bare-minimum and does not declare README/license/authors or test/dev extras. |

**Score:** 6/10.

**Estimated rewrite/significant-change size:** about 220 lines. Most of that is parser hardening, current-ingest replacement semantics, alias lifecycle cleanup, and negative-path tests.

**PR approval:** No. The code is tidy and the fixture-driven tests pass (`58 passed`), but I would block this as-is because malformed inputs can still crash ingest and normal re-ingest workflows can leave materially wrong data in the database.

issues.description: Re-ingesting changed input only upserts and never removes rows missing from the latest input tree, so stale results remain in reports.
Malformed XML raises ET.ParseError and crashes ingest instead of producing a structured warning.
Empty run_id, model, or task values are accepted; empty run IDs collide under UNIQUE(run_id, source) and silently overwrite rows.
Non-finite scores like NaN are treated as numeric and can abort ingest with a SQLite NOT NULL integrity error.
model_aliases is append-only while warnings/stats are replaced, so alias reports can include stale spellings from prior ingests.
Format A parses CSV one physical line at a time, corrupting valid CSV records with quoted embedded newlines.
CSV and JSONL inputs are read fully into memory, creating avoidable OOM/DoS risk for large harness outputs.
Format B assumes truthy metrics is a dict; malformed JSON such as metrics=[1] crashes with AttributeError.
Empty-directory ingest returns an error only after creating/mutating the SQLite database.
Package metadata is bare-minimum and does not declare README/license/authors or test/dev extras.
